title: Bounded-time memory copy
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathrm{lim}$ specify word, space, and depth limits. Suppose the program entry at $p$ is the copy routine, the space limit is at most the word limit, and the source interval $[\mathrm{src},\mathrm{src}+n)$ and destination interval $[\mathrm{dst},\mathrm{dst}+n)$ lie within the space bound and are disjoint. Then, starting with arguments $(\mathrm{src},\mathrm{dst},n)$ and memory $\mu$, that routine has an execution at depth $d$ of cost at most $16n+6$ whose final memory agrees with $\mu$ outside the destination interval and satisfies $\mu'(\mathrm{dst}+i)=\mu(\mathrm{src}+i)$ for every $i<n$.
hypotheses_covered: The source and destination intervals are disjoint
